target: Je marchais dans la rue quand j'ai vu un vieil ami.
english: I was walking down the street when I saw an old friend.
tip: Imparfait sets the scene (marchais), passé composé introduces a new event (ai vu).

target: Nous riions beaucoup ensemble.
english: We used to laugh a lot together.
tip: Être is the only verb with an irregular imparfait stem: et-.

target: Elle me l'a dit hier.
english: She told me yesterday.
tip: Double pronouns: me + le becomes me l'. Order: me/te/se/nous/vous + le/la/les.

target: Nous le connaissons depuis l'enfance.
english: We've known him since childhood.
tip: Object pronouns go before the conjugated verb.

target: Nous mangions ensemble tous les dimanches.
english: We used to eat together every Sunday.
tip: 'Tous les dimanches' (every Sunday) is a clear habit marker → imparfait is the right tense.

target: Elle dormait quand l'alarme s'est déclenchée.
english: She was sleeping when the alarm went off.
tip: Imparfait for ongoing action interrupted by passé composé: 'elle dormait' (ongoing) + 'l'alarme s'est déclenchée' (sudden event).

target: Tu étais content de ton travail ?
english: Were you happy with your job?
tip: Être in imparfait: j'etais, tu etais, il/elle etait, nous etions, vous etiez, ils/elles etaient.

target: Tu voyageais souvent pour le travail ?
english: Did you use to travel often for work?
tip: Imparfait for polite requests: 'je voulais vous demander...' = I wanted to ask you... (softer than present).

target: Je les connais tous par leur prenom.
english: I know them all by their first name.
tip: Direct object pronouns (le/la/les) sit before the verb: `je le vois` (I see him/it), not `je vois le`. Before vowels they elide: `je l'aime`.

target: Nous écoutions la radio pendant le trajet.
english: We used to listen to the radio during the trip.
tip: 'Être' is the only verb with an irregular imparfait stem: ét- (j'étais). All others use the nous-form.

target: Il pouvait courir très vite à cette époque.
english: He used to be able to run very fast at that time.
tip: Pouvoir in imparfait describes a past ability or possibility: il pouvait = he could.

target: Je me lève à sept heures tous les matins.
english: I get up at seven o'clock every morning.
tip: Reflexive verbs use a pronoun: me, te, se, nous, vous, se. Je me lève = I get myself up.

target: Tu étais au bureau quand l'orage a éclaté ?
english: Were you at the office when the storm broke out?
tip: 'Être' in imparfait (tu étais = you were) for the backdrop, then passé composé for the event (l'orage a éclaté).

target: Tu avais faim quand tu es rentré du travail ?
english: Were you hungry when you came home from work?
tip: States and feelings use imparfait (avais faim). Completed actions use PC (es rentre).

target: Tu avais dix ans quand tu as déménagé en France ?
english: Were you ten years old when you moved to France?
tip: Age in the past uses imparfait (avais). Moving is a completed event: PC (as demenage).

target: Dehors il fait un froid glacial ce matin.
english: Outside it's freezing cold this morning.
tip: Affirmative imperative: verb + direct pronoun + indirect pronoun.

target: Elle faisait la cuisine quand elle s'est coupé le doigt.
english: She was cooking when she cut her finger.
tip: Reflexive verbs in PC: elle s'est coupé. Imparfait for the background action.

target: Je conduisais quand j'ai entendu la nouvelle à la radio.
english: I was driving when I heard the news on the radio.
tip: Driving (ongoing, imparfait) vs hearing news (punctual event, passé composé). The tenses work together.

target: Merci pour votre aide.
english: Thank you for your help.
tip: Pour after merci expresses what you are thankful for.

target: Je me suis trompé de route.
english: I took the wrong road.
tip: Se tromper = to make a mistake. Je me suis trompé: agreement with masculine subject.

target: Tu t'es repose ce week-end ?
english: Did you rest this weekend?
tip: Reflexive pronouns: me, te, se, nous, vous, se.

target: Il pleuvait quand nous sommes sortis.
english: It was raining when we went out.
tip: Background weather (imparfait) vs completed action (passé composé).

target: Elle s'est blessée en faisant du ski.
english: She hurt herself while skiing.
tip: Se blesser = to hurt oneself. Passé composé with être: elle s'est blessee.

target: Ils se sont perdus dans la forêt.
english: They got lost in the forest.
tip: Reflexive pronoun goes before the verb: 'je me lève'. In negative: 'je ne me lève pas' – pronoun stays with the verb.

target: Je me suis couche tard hier soir.
english: I went to bed late last night.
tip: With body parts, no agreement on past participle: elle s'est lavé les mains.

target: Tu te souviens de notre première rencontre ?
english: Do you remember our first meeting?
tip: Se souvenir de = to remember. The reflexive pronoun is essential for meaning.

target: Le repas a été paye par mon frère.
english: The meal was paid for by my brother.
tip: 'Par' for frequency: 'trois fois par semaine' = three times per week.

target: Tu travaillais déjà ici quand l'entreprise a déménagé ?
english: Were you already working here when the company moved?
tip: If both actions are simultaneous and ongoing, both use imparfait: 'je lisais pendant qu'elle cuisinait'.

target: Il faut que l'on prenne le train de six heures.
english: We need to take the six o'clock train.
tip: After expressions of will/necessity/emotion + `que`, French switches to subjunctive. `Je veux que tu viennes` (not viens) = 'I want you to come'.

target: Ils jouaient dans le jardin quand il a commencé à pleuvoir.
english: They were playing in the garden when it started raining.
tip: 'Quand' or 'lorsque' + passé composé marks the interrupting event. The other action is imparfait.

target: Elle se brosse les cheveux chaque soir.
english: She brushes her hair every evening.
tip: Not always reflexive in English: `se souvenir` = to remember, `se dépêcher` = to hurry. If the dictionary form starts with `se`, you need a matching pronoun.

target: Je me suis installé dans mon nouveau bureau.
english: I settled into my new office.
tip: In passé composé, reflexive past participles DON'T agree with indirect objects: 'elles se sont parlé' (no -e, 'se' is indirect).

target: Nous cherchons un hôtel qui ait une piscine.
english: We're looking for a hotel that has a pool.
tip: Subjunctive in relative clauses when the antecedent is not yet identified or uncertain.

target: Il faut que nous nous adaptions aux nouvelles technologies.
english: We need to adapt to new technologies.
tip: Trigger phrases: `il faut que`, `je veux que`, `bien que`, `pour que`, `avant que`. Subjonctif endings: -e/-es/-e/-ions/-iez/-ent for most. Drop the -e on irregular verbs to find the stem.

target: Il faut que tu te reposes si tu veux guérir.
english: You need to rest if you want to recover.
tip: If the main clause is a wish, doubt, fear, or judgment, the `que` clause goes subjunctive. The action is hypothetical, even if it sounds factual.

target: Il faut que tout le monde soit prêt à huit heures.
english: Everyone needs to be ready at eight o'clock.
tip: After expressions of will/necessity/emotion + `que`, French switches to subjunctive. `Je veux que tu viennes` (not viens) = 'I want you to come'.

target: Il finira par comprendre.
english: He will end up understanding.
tip: Finir par = to end up doing something. Par introduces the eventual outcome.

target: Je ne le sais pas.
english: I don't know it.
tip: In negation, the pronoun stays before the verb: ne + pronoun + verb + pas.

target: Tu en as assez ?
english: Do you have enough of it?
tip: `en` = 'of it / of them / some' – replaces `de + noun` or a quantity. `Tu veux du café? Oui, j'en veux` (Yes, I want some).

target: Elle le connaît depuis longtemps.
english: She has known him for a long time.
tip: `le` = m, `la` = f, `les` = pl. Match the gender/number of what they replace. In compound tenses, this pronoun also triggers participle agreement.

target: C'est pour toi, joyeux anniversaire !
english: It's for you, happy birthday!
tip: Pour indicates purpose or recipient: pour toi = for you.

target: Ce cadeau est pour les enfants.
english: This gift is for the children.
tip: 'Pour' indicates the beneficiary: 'pour les enfants' = for the children.

target: Elle lui parle souvent au téléphone.
english: She often talks to him/her on the phone.
tip: Lui is an indirect object pronoun meaning to him or to her. Placed before the verb.

target: Elles se sont assises à la terrasse.
english: They sat on the terrace.
tip: S'asseoir: elles se sont assises. Irregular with feminine plural agreement.

target: Nous avons appris la nouvelle par hasard.
english: We learned the news by chance.
tip: Par hasard = by chance. Par is used in many expressions of manner.

target: Tu en as combien chez toi ?
english: How many do you have at home?
tip: After numbers and `beaucoup/peu/assez`, `en` is required: `j'en ai trois` (I have three [of them]). English drops the 'of them'; French keeps `en`.

target: Nous nous promenons dans le parc chaque dimanche.
english: We take a walk in the park every Sunday.
tip: Se promener = to take a walk. Nous nous promenons: first nous is subject, second is reflexive pronoun.

target: La maison a été construite par mon grand-père.
english: The house was built by my grandfather.
tip: 'Par' with passive construction: 'construite par mon grand-père'. Note agreement: construite (feminine for 'maison').

target: Il travaillé pour une grande entreprise.
english: He worked for a large company.
tip: Pour + employer = for (working for someone or something).

target: Tu t'es bien amuse hier soir ?
english: Did you have fun last night?
tip: In questions with passé composé, the reflexive pronoun stays before être: tu t'es amuse.

target: Ils ont voyagé par avion jusqu'à Tokyo.
english: They traveled by plane to Tokyo.
tip: Par + means of transport: par avion, par bateau, par le train.

target: Nous avons acheté des fleurs pour notre mère.
english: We bought flowers for our mother.
tip: Pour + person = for someone (recipient or beneficiary).

target: Elle s'est habillée rapidement pour partir au travail.
english: She got dressed quickly to leave for work.
tip: In passé composé, reflexive verbs use être: elle s'est habillee. The participle agrees with the subject.

target: Il en a acheté plusieurs au marché ce matin.
english: He bought several at the market this morning.
tip: After numbers and `beaucoup/peu/assez`, `en` is required: `j'en ai trois` (I have three [of them]). English drops the 'of them'; French keeps `en`.

target: Il a été félicité par ses collègues.
english: He was congratulated by his colleagues.
tip: 'Par' after passive 'être + past participle': 'félicité par ses collègues'.

target: Il la cherché partout.
english: He looked for her everywhere.
tip: With infinitives, pronouns go before the infinitive: 'je veux le voir' (I want to see him).

target: Tu lui ressembles beaucoup.
english: You look a lot like him/her.
tip: Ressembler a quelqu'un: lui replaces a + person.

target: Il me comprend très bien.
english: He understands me very well.
tip: Indirect object pronouns (lui, leur) replace a + person.

target: Nous les attendons depuis midi.
english: We've been waiting for them since noon.
tip: 'Les' replaces plural direct objects: 'nous les attendons' = we wait for them.

target: Elle a terminé par un dessert.
english: She finished with a dessert.
tip: Terminer par = to finish with. Par introduces what comes at the end.
